MEASURE — Reordering r67's 768 hidden channels by measured activation frequency is lossless and makes empty vector blocks much more common, but the proposed standalone block skip is slower on both kernel widths. Across 2,902 actual heldout positions, empty per-perspective blocks rose from 13.81% to 35.66% for 16-unit AVX2 vectors, and from 1.86% to 23.37% for 32-unit AVX-512 vectors. Simultaneously empty blocks rose from 3.11% to 23.54% and from 0.11% to 14.74%. Higher sparsity is real; its bookkeeping costs more than these multiply-adds on this host.

On the 48 disjoint root clusters, the 256-bit reordered sparse kernel took a median 39.20ns/output vs native stock dense 35.06ns; median within-cluster time INCREASE 10.94% [10.03,11.77]. At 512 bits it took 38.18ns vs 28.11ns, an increase 35.06% [33.31,36.61]. Dense reordered alone was within 1% in both cases. The +10% time-saving threshold fails; no whole-engine pilot or plan addition. These are local hot output-dot timings, on a machine compiled for x86-64-v4, not full search or the AVX-512 fused update that Neon is investigating independently.

All hidden integer accumulators matched after applying the permutation and raw sums matched stock scalar, stock dense and both alternative kernels in every root; unchanged bits included benchmark 11/13 at 226187/616966. Exact integer tests included all-zero, saturated positive and negative upper-limit output weights, mixed signs and int16 extremes, returning the expected ±12,684,556,800 wide values when all terms had one sign. Weight checksum and full permutation below. Predeclared calibration, scope and tests are 094753Z. Compile unchanged GNU stock x86-64-v4 objects from 094111Z; for each heldout position copy actual side-to-move and opposing int16 accumulator vectors after stock refresh. Measure the ordinary native dispatch to output_sum_with and the alternative, on exactly those same arrays/heads. Alternative tests signed lanes >0 separately in each perspective, skips when none, otherwise uses the same int16 clamp and multiply-add with widened 64-bit final sum. Split 384 source game IDs by ID modulo 48, 96 repeats per cell, 8 cycles with forward and reversed 8-cell order rotated by group+cycle; all output sums observed and checked, CPU affinity fixed. Median of 16 timings at each group; bootstrap 10,000 of the 48 independent groups, seed 202611230947. Record both ns and ratios so relative increases can be recounted without dividing two unrelated medians.
